text:
sachin: heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak p99 for gen models jumped from ~220ms to ~480ms on the hosted tier. noticed this around 13:40 UTC, reproduces on canary.
elaine: ugh, link to the job? :eyes:
sachin: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf-runs/1718012000 — profiler attached in the job artifacts. short summary: microbatching rate dropped, KV cache miss rate increased ~3x for long chats, and kernel fallback to fp16_gemm happened frequently.
maria: do you have the per-gpu utilization traces? wondering if this is GPU saturation or headroom issue.
perf-bot: perf run 1718012000 completed. p50: 120ms, p95: 310ms, p99: 480ms, throughput: -12% vs baseline. profiling: see /artifacts/1718012000/profile.html
sachin: attached small excerpt from nvprof and our internal tracer:
```
[TRACE] model=redwood-7b variant=cpu_optimized_kernels
queue_depth: mean=8.1, tail=54
microbatch_size: mean=4 (target 8)
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.36
kernel_switches: 23 -> 89
GPU util: 68% -> 74% (spikey, high variance)
```
elaine: interesting — GPU util increased slightly but microbatch size decreased. could be that kernel selection has more expensive per-token paths for certain sequence lengths causing lower batching efficiency.
maria: my read: two things combined: selector prefers low-latency kernel for short sequences but switches to a degenerate path for long-history chats, which hurts batching and causes more KV lookups (misses) because of cache fragmentation.
tom: i think the core tradeoff we need to revisit is latency SLO (p95/p99) vs throughput. if we aim for strict p99 400ms, we might need to lower target utilization to keep headroom for bursts.
elaine: agreed. current autoscaler targets 85% target_util which is fine for average but not for tail-sensitive routes.
sachin: proposal: implement adaptive microbatch sizing + admission-control tokens for hot endpoints. heuristics:
```
# pseudocode
if route.slo == 'latency-p99-tight':
  target_util = 0.6
else:
  target_util = 0.78

# microbatch adapt
microbatch = clamp(1, int(queue_depth/4), max_microbatch)
if observed_p99 > slo_p99: microbatch = max(1, microbatch-1)
```
maria: also add a KV cache coalescing pass — when we detect many small caches for same conversation, try to compact or pin prefixes to reduce misses.
tom: +1. but we should measure the unit-cost impact: lower util -> more cost. ops-bot can we get an estimate of delta?
ops-bot: estimated delta for moving avg util 78% -> 62%: +22% infra cost for affected pools, expected p99 improvement ~35-50% depending on workload.
elaine: can we be surgical? e.g., only apply conservative util targets for routes with high tail sensitivity: chat-api, assist-router, low-priority batch routes keep 80+.
sachin: yes, per-route admission control tokens and a circuit-breaker for queue depth > 200. if queueing grows we shed low-priority requests (embeddings batch, non-interactive). also fallback to quantized kernel if microbatch > threshold.
maria: we should also avoid oscillations — implement hysteresis on kernel selector: require sustained perf delta > 10% for 2 minutes before flip.
tom: for postmortem: plan a canary where we revert selector for one model family OR tune thresholds; compare p95/p99 and throughput over 24h. add synthetic tail load to catch burst behaviour.
elaine: add dashboards: per-route p50/p95/p99, queue_depth distribution, microbatch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_variant_count. wire alerts on p99 breach and sustained queue_depth > 30s.
perf-bot: scheduled an A/B perf run: baseline vs tuned-adaptive-microbatch on canary cluster at 16:00 UTC. artifacts will be posted automatically.
sachin: next steps I can do: roll out admission-control prototype + hysteresis + dashboard panels. can someone own KV coalescing change? Maria?
maria: i can take KV coalescing (small refactor in cache manager) — aiming for PR by EOD tomorrow.
tom: I'll take the canary experiment orchestration and cost impact analysis.
elaine: I'll update autoscaler policy to support per-route util targets and add the hysteresis knobs.
sachin: cool. long-term we also want smarter kernel-selection: cost model that considers microbatch efficiency and KV cache locality rather than pure latency per-call. that'll reduce these flip-flops.
maria: quick note: for the canary add a synthetic long-chat scenario (seq_len=8192, prefix hit ratio=0.2) — that's where regressions showed up.
tom: noted. will include synthetic.
sachin: thanks all — ping here with PR links and perf artifacts. :thumbsup:
